title: The 1.3B model people preferred to GPT-3
summary: In OpenAI's InstructGPT paper, human evaluators preferred a 1.3B parameter model over the 175B parameter GPT-3.

beats.say: People preferred a model one hundred times smaller than G.P.T. three.
Making a model bigger does not automatically make it follow instructions.
beats.cap: Bigger is not inherently better at following intent

beats.say: Parameters are the adjustable numbers inside a model.
The small model got extra training: labelers wrote and ranked answers.
beats.cap: Extra step: fine-tuned with human feedback

beats.say: In human evaluations, its outputs were preferred over the big model's.
beats.cap: Human evaluators preferred the small model

beats.say: That is one hundred times fewer parameters, according to the paper.
The exact ratio is closer to one hundred thirty five.
It was not larger. It was better aimed at what people wanted.
Training on what people prefer can beat adding parameters.
beats.cap: Human feedback can beat raw size

beats.say: One hundred times smaller. Still preferred.

claims.note: InstructGPT paper abstract: 'outputs from the 1.3B parameter InstructGPT model are preferred to outputs from the 175B GPT-3'
Hugging Face paper page: preferred 'despite having 100x fewer parameters'

facts.claim: Human evaluators preferred outputs from the 1.3B InstructGPT model to outputs from the 175B GPT-3
facts.note: Abstract: 'outputs from the 1.3B parameter InstructGPT model are preferred to outputs from the 175B GPT-3'

facts.claim: Making language models bigger does not inherently make them better at following a user's intent
facts.note: Abstract, first sentence: 'Making language models bigger does not inherently make them better'

facts.claim: InstructGPT was fine-tuned with labeler demonstrations and rankings of model outputs
facts.note: Abstract: a dataset of labeler demonstrations of the desired behavior and a dataset of rankings of model outputs; fine-tuning with human feedback

youtube.hook: In OpenAI's InstructGPT paper, human evaluators preferred outputs from a 1.3B parameter model over outputs from the 175B parameter GPT-3. The small model had been fine-tuned with human feedback.

instagram.caption: A model 100 times smaller than GPT-3 was preferred by human evaluators. Size was not the deciding factor.

tiktok.caption: A 1.3B model beat GPT-3's 175B in human preference.
